description: Composite figure of mixed type; four of its five panels are supplied and they are of two kinds. (b) is a Holloman's plot, ln σ (×10³ MPa, y-axis ticked 6.4–7.2) versus ln ε (x-axis ticked −5, −4, −3, −2, −1), carrying three coloured curves for the tensile samples: blue A5 (uppermost, spanning ln ε ≈ −5 to −1.6), green A15 (middle), magenta A30 (lowest). Each curve is split into two stages by thin grey linear fits with printed exponents: A5 n = 0.069 (initial) then n = 0.179; A15 n = 0.064 then n = 0.25; A30 n = 0.054 then n = 0.27. (c), (d) and (e) are optical micrographs of the deformed tensile gauge of A5, A15 and A30 respectively, each with a 50 µm scale bar, a green sample label, blue double arrows marking elongated aligned "B2 stringer" bands in a lighter matrix, and orange arrows marking a "micro-crack" ("microcrack" in (d)) at the specimen edge. The group argues that the two-stage strain-hardening response of B2 + γ persists after annealing with the second-stage n rising from A5 to A30, while the micrographs show micro-cracks pinned at the stringer bands, i.e. reduced crack susceptibility. Panel (a), the engineering stress–strain curves named in the caption, is not supplied.
measured_quantities: strain hardening exponent n (dimensionless, two per sample)

observations.observation: Panel (b) is a Holloman's plot with vertical axis labelled lnσ, ×10³ MPa (ticked 6.4–7.2) and horizontal axis labelled lnε (ticked −5, −4, −3, −2, −1).
Three curves appear in (b), labelled A5 (blue, highest), A15 (green, middle) and A30 (magenta, lowest), each resolved into two fitted stages.
Printed strain-hardening exponents in (b) are n = 0.069 and n = 0.179 for A5, n = 0.064 and n = 0.25 for A15, and n = 0.054 and n = 0.27 for A30; in every case the second value is the larger.
Thin grey straight lines accompany each curve stage in (b), representing the best linear fits of lnσ versus lnε.
Panels (c), (d) and (e) each carry a 50 µm scale bar and a green sample label (A5, A15, A30 respectively).
In (c), (d) and (e) the microstructure is a strongly banded, aligned two-phase structure, with blue double arrows labelling the dark elongated features as 'B2 stringer'.
Orange arrows label a micro-crack at the specimen edge in (c) ('micro-crack'), (d) ('microcrack', no hyphen) and (e) ('micro-crack').
The caption states that (a) shows engineering stress–strain curves of samples processed under modified HR, CR and annealing for 5–30 mins; this panel is not present in the supplied group.
The caption identifies (b) as Holloman's plot demonstrating the strain hardening exponent (n) for various samples.
The caption identifies (c), (d) and (e) as optical micrographs of the deformed tensile gauge showing reduced crack susceptibility in the modified A5, A15 and A30 respectively.

The citing text states that the strain hardening exponent is calculated from true stress (σ)–true strain (ε) curves using σ = kεⁿ in logarithmic form, and that the value from the best linear fits of lnσ versus lnε is initially low due to yield point elongation (YPE), followed by a steady rise through combined plastic deformation of γ and B2.
The citing text states that strain partitioning between softer γ and harder B2 reduces the overall strain hardening exponent to 0.19–0.27 by a rule of mixture.

The citing text states that refinement of the B2 stringer bands reduces the stringer band fraction from 16% to 11%, and that the enhanced austenite fraction between thinner bands delays crack propagation and stringer band decohesion by absorbing plastic strain.

The citing text attributes the higher YS of the less annealed A5 (YS increases to 1 GPa) to residual dislocations left behind by high-speed HR, and reports a toughness of 1.72 kJ mol⁻¹ (238 J cm⁻³) in A30 (inset, Figure 6a) — neither number is verifiable from the supplied panels.

Optical micrograph of the deformed tensile gauge of A5 with a 50 µm scale bar; blue arrows point to 'B2 stringer' bands, orange arrows to a 'micro-crack' near an external edge/corner.
